c.tagline: Japan's volcano city, where an active Sakurajima smokes across the bay.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares start around ¥620. There is no Uber-style street ride-hailing here — taxis are picked up at ranks, hailed on the street, or booked by phone or the GO/DiDi apps; plentiful downtown but thin late at night.

emergency.note: Dial 110 for police and 119 for fire and ambulance. English-speaking operators can be limited, so a translation app or Japan's official Safety Tips app helps.

avoid.reason: Tenmonkan's bar district has occasional touts late at night; otherwise just usual city awareness.

hood_desc: Kagoshima's buzzing downtown of covered shopping arcades, izakayas, ramen bars, and nightlife around the Tenmonkan tram stop; the most central and lively base for first-timers who want everything within walking distance.

The modern transport hub around JR Kagoshima-Chuo Station (the Kyushu Shinkansen terminus), ringed by the Amu Plaza mall and Ferris wheel, newer restaurants, and easy tram/bus links; convenient and practical for arrivals and departures.

The breezy bayfront strip around Dolphin Port, the City Aquarium, and the Sakurajima Ferry Terminal, with casual seafood spots, foot baths, and evening ferry-watching across Kinko Bay to the volcano; relaxed and scenic.

A historic coastal area on the northeastern edge of the city built around Sengan-en, the grand Shimazu clan daimyo garden that frames Sakurajima and Kinko Bay, plus the Shoko Shuseikan industrial-heritage museum; quiet and sightseeing-focused.

A leafy 107-meter hilltop district crowned by the Shiroyama Observatory (the classic Sakurajima viewpoint) and site of the last stand of the 1877 Satsuma Rebellion; calm, green, and home to onsen resort hotels above the bustle.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.pay: Both tram lines charge a flat ¥170 (~$1.15) per ride (¥80 children), paid in cash or by tapping a nationwide IC card (Suica, ICOCA) or the local RapiCa/Iwasaki card; the same IC cards work on city buses. A 1-Day Tram/Bus/City View Bus pass costs about ¥600 (~$4), sold at the tourist office and on board.
transit.hours: Trams and city buses run from roughly 6am to around 11pm; the Sakurajima Ferry runs 24 hours, every 10-15 minutes by day and about hourly overnight (13-min crossing).
